column3: The Hebrew says they sit before him in a narrow place; BSB describes meeting with him in a place too small for them.
The Hebrew leaves the final speaker unnamed; BSB supplies Elisha.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the traveler unnamed and says they cut the trees; BSB supplies Elisha and adds began.
The Hebrew calls the falling object the iron; BSB specifies the iron axe head.
The Hebrew leaves the cutter unnamed; BSB repeats the man of God.
The Hebrew says lift for yourself and leaves the taker unnamed; BSB says lift it out and supplies the man.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “not once and not twice” and identifies the warning source as the man of God; BSB says “Time and again” and names Elisha.
The Hebrew says the heart of the king was troubled; BSB says the king became enraged.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker and the man reported in Dothan unnamed; BSB supplies the king and Elisha.
The Hebrew leaves the sender unnamed; BSB supplies the king of Aram.
The Hebrew calls the speaker his servant and leaves the addressee unnamed; BSB uses he and supplies Elisha.
The Hebrew leaves the respondent unnamed; BSB supplies Elisha.
The Hebrew uses singular mountain; BSB uses plural hills.
The Hebrew leaves those descending unnamed and calls them this nation; BSB supplies the Arameans and says these people.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they saw and behold, in the midst of Samaria; BSB describes looking around and discovering their location.
The Hebrew repeats striking without an explicit killing verb; BSB twice asks whether to kill them.
The Hebrew joins sword and bow with and and says bread; BSB uses or and food.
The Hebrew leaves the feast-maker unnamed; BSB supplies the king.
The Hebrew coordinates marching up and besieging as actions; BSB makes besieging the purpose of marching up.
The Hebrew leaves the silver unit implicit; BSB supplies shekels for both prices.
